title: Sort Vowels in a String
summary: Given a string s, rearrange it to form a new string t where all consonants stay in their original positions and all vowels are sorted in ascending ASCII order.
statement: Given a string s, rearrange it to form a new string t where all consonants stay in their original positions and all vowels are sorted in ascending ASCII order. Vowels include 'a', 'e', 'i', 'o', 'u' in both lowercase and uppercase. Consonants are all other letters.
constraints: Keep every consonant at its original index.
Sort all English vowels by character code and place them back into vowel positions.
hints: Sort vowel characters by their ordinary character-code order.
Iterate through s, replacing only vowel positions from the sorted iterator.
The fixed consonant positions and sorted sequence uniquely determine the required result.
editorial: The fixed consonant positions and sorted sequence uniquely determine the required result.

tests.explanation: The vowel codes sort as E,O,e,e, producing lEOtcede.
There are no vowels, so the string is unchanged.
